Scheme 1. Activation Modes of Terminal Alkyne under
Transition Metal (TM) Catalysis
The catalytic copper species typically activates the terminal
alkyne to produce a copper−acetylide species and also
activates the diazoacetate to produce a copper−carbene
species. Terminal alkyne undergoes deprotonation to deliver
the copper−acetylide, which subsequently reacts with the
diazoacetate. Alternatively, the copper catalyst may first
activate the diazoacetate to produce the copper−carbene,
which then engages with the terminal alkyne. Although Sun
and co-workers have made significant progress to elucidate the
mechanism of this reaction, two major problems are still
unclear. First, establishing a general mechanistic scheme is
challenging due to the involvement of diferent activation
modes. Second, the molecular origin of the high stereo-
selectivity requires further clarification. As a result, our interest
was drawn to investigating this copper-catalyzed asymmetric
synthesis of a tetrasubstituted allene. Theoretical mechanistic
analysis of transition-metal-catalyzed reactions<sup>32−37</sup>
is at the
center of our research. Therefore, in this study, we employed
density functional theory (DFT), which is a robust computa-
tional method for mechanistic investigations,<sup>38−49</sup>
to theoret-
ically investigate the mechanism of the copper-catalyzed cross-
coupling reaction between a terminal alkyne and diazoacetate.
In particular, we intend to elucidate the activation mode in
detail, specifically whether copper−acetylide or copper−
carbene serves as the key intermediate.

2. COMPUTATIONAL METHODS
All quantum chemical calculations were performed using the Gaussian
09 software package.<sup>50</sup> Geometry optimizations were carried out with
the M06-L functional.<sup>51,52</sup> The 6-31G(d, p) basis set<sup>53,54</sup>
was
employed for the C, H, O, N, and F atoms, while the SDD basis
set<sup>55,56</sup> was used for the Cu atom. Solvation efects were incorporated
via the continuum solvation model IEF-PCM,<sup>57,58</sup>
using dichloro-
methane (DCM, ε = 8.93) as the solvent. Harmonic vibrational
analysis verifies that the stationary points are characterized as minima
with no imaginary frequency or transition states with one and only
one imaginary frequency, respectively. To refine the calculated energy,
single-point calculations with a larger basis set were then performed
based on these optimized structures, by using the M06-L functional
with the Def2-TZVP basis set.<sup>59,60</sup> The free energies reported in this
work were calculated based on the single point energy at the M06-L/
def2-TZVP level, including the Gibbs free energy thermal correction
obtained from vibrational analysis at the geometry optimization level.
For disclosing the origin of stereoselectivity, the Multiwfn software
package<sup>61</sup> is used to generate the interaction wave functions, which
are then visualized through VMD

4. CONCLUSIONS
The DFT method was performed to explore the mechanism of
the cross-coupling reaction of diazoacetate and alkyne
catalyzed by Cu(I) species toward the synthesis of chiral
allenes. The proposed pathway comprises five key steps: (1)
alkynation of the Cu(I) species to form copper−acetylide
species, (2) carbenation of the diazoacetate to generate
copper−carbene acetylide species, (3) carbene insertion into
the copper−carbene acetylide species, yielding a propargyl
copper intermediate, (4) an intramolecular aldol reaction that
releases the allenoate copper species, and (5) protonation of
the allenoate copper species to aford the final chiral exocyclic
α-allenol and regenerate the active copper catalyst. The
carbenation step was identified as both the stereoselectivity-
and rate-determining step, with an energy barrier of 27.6 kcal/
mol. DFT calculations indicate that the copper−carbene
pathway exhibits an overall energy barrier of 44.8 kcal/mol
and is thus energetically disfavored. An NCI analysis revealed
the significance of interactions between diazoacetate and the
indane group of the Box ligand in governing the stereo-
selectivity. A range of chiral Box ligands was also evaluated,
and the presence of an indane group was found to promote
high stereoselectivity, consistent with experimental findings.
Computational results demonstrate that when an indane group
is present on the Box ligand, the conventional pathway
comprising alkynylation, carbenation, carbene insertion, aldol
reaction, and protonation is energetically favorable. The
present study enhances the mechanistic understanding of the
cross-coupling reaction between diazoacetate and alkyne
catalyzed by copper and ofers a theoretical foundation for
guiding further experimental studies.
